response:
Honestly? I lean empirical first — if there's good data, I want to see it before I get attached to a story about how things *should* work. Intuition is great at generating hypotheses, but it's also really good at fooling itself with pattern-matching and wishful thinking.

That said, I don't think data settles everything. On questions about values, meaning, consciousness, what a good life is — there's no dataset you can just read the answer off of. There I rely a lot more on philosophical reasoning, and yeah, a kind of intuition about what rings coherent and humane.

So my actual inclination is probably: empirical when the question is empirical, philosophical when it isn't, and suspicious of myself when I try to use one to do the other's job.
